items.title: Deterministic preprocessing for empirical covariance concentration

source.edition: Tropp, An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, 2015
source.anchor: matrix Bernstein setup and sample-covariance applications
source.attribution: Samplinglib isolates the deterministic rank-one decomposition and bounded symmetric summand conditions used before applying a matrix concentration theorem.

items.statement: A bounded finite sample and a bounded symmetric population second-moment operator determine centered symmetric rank-one summands whose normalized sum is the empirical error and whose individual operator norms are at most twice the squared radius.
assumptions: A real inner-product space and a nonempty finite sample index.
A nonnegative radius B bounding every sample vector.
A symmetric population continuous linear operator with norm at most B².

obligations.label: Define the normalized finite-sample rank-one operator average
Identify the exact operator norm of a self outer product
Prove the exact centered decomposition, summand symmetry, and 2B² bound

bindings.boundary: Definition only; no probability law, centering convention, independence, or concentration is asserted.

assumption_deltas.source: Sample-covariance arguments average rank-one outer products.
assumption_deltas.lean: Samplinglib defines the finite-type normalized second-moment operator with an explicit empty-sample inverse-cardinality convention.
assumption_deltas.reason: The downstream theorem assumes a nonempty index; the total definition remains meaningful on every finite type.

bindings.boundary: Deterministic operator norm identity only; no random-matrix statement is inferred.

assumption_deltas.source: A self outer product has operator norm ‖x‖².
assumption_deltas.lean: The theorem proves the same identity for Mathlib's continuous rank-one operator on an arbitrary real inner-product space.
assumption_deltas.reason: The domains and constant are unchanged.

bindings.boundary: No independence, expectation identity, matrix variance proxy, noncommutative concentration theorem, probability tail, or sample-complexity conclusion is asserted.

assumption_deltas.source: Matrix Bernstein applications first express the empirical error as a sum of centered self-adjoint random matrices and bound each summand.
assumption_deltas.lean: The theorem assumes a nonempty finite deterministic sample, symmetry and norm control of the supplied population operator, and proves exactly the decomposition, symmetry, and 2B² summand bound.
assumption_deltas.reason: The probabilistic concentration step is deliberately outside this deterministic prerequisite.
